title: Shared link "Show metadata" is not applied to POST /search/metadata, leaking EXIF and GPS
summary:
# "Show metadata" is not applied to POST /search/metadata, so shared links leak EXIF and GPS

## Summary

A shared album link created with "Show metadata" turned off still returns the full unredacted asset record
from `POST /search/metadata`. One unauthenticated request with the link key yields GPS latitude and
longitude, reverse-geocoded city and country, camera make and model, capture time, the original filename,
the on-disk path and the owner UUID, for every asset in the album.

This is a response-sanitization gap, not an authorization bypass. Object scope is intact and I want to be
clear about that up front.

Introduced in v3.0.2 by commit `655cd01d5` on 2026-07-08. Present in v3.0.3, v3.1.0 and main at `a9a99cff`.
Confirmed on the released v3.1.0 image, `sourceCommit 8aa95c67`.

## The invariant is yours, written as a test

`e2e/src/specs/server/api/shared-link.e2e-spec.ts:280`

```ts
it('should not return metadata for album shared link without metadata', async () => {
  ...
  const asset = body.assets[0];
  expect(asset).not.toHaveProperty('exifInfo');
  expect(asset).not.toHaveProperty('fileCreatedAt');
  expect(asset).not.toHaveProperty('originalFilename');
  expect(asset).not.toHaveProperty('originalPath');
});
```

`POST /search/metadata` with the same class of key returns all four. I am not asserting a preference here,
just showing that an assertion you already wrote is violated on a different route.

The clamp is enforced in seven places server-side. Two push it down into the SQL projection at
`asset.repository.ts:836` and `:930`, and `asset-media.service.ts:289` swaps the real filename for the asset
UUID in a thumbnail's Content-Disposition. The project works hard at this. One sink was missed.

## Where it is missed

`server/src/services/asset.service.ts` applies three clamps for a share key:

```ts
if (auth.sharedLink && !auth.sharedLink.showExif) {
  return mapAsset(asset, { stripMetadata: true, withStack: true, auth });
}
const data = mapAsset(asset, { withStack: true, auth });
if (auth.sharedLink) { delete data.owner; }
```

`server/src/services/search.service.ts:99` ends with none of them:

```ts
return this.mapResponse(items, hasNextPage ? (page + 1).toString() : null, { auth });
```

`mapAsset` never inspects `auth.sharedLink` on its own. `stripMetadata` is only ever set by the caller, and
`grep -rn "stripMetadata" server/src/` finds exactly three call sites. `search.service.ts` is not one.

## The commit that opened it

`655cd01d5`, "search metadata for album shared links", is the commit that first let share keys reach this
endpoint. It added the object-scope half and not the sanitization half:

```diff
-  @Authenticated({ permission: Permission.AssetRead })
+  @Authenticated({ permission: Permission.AssetRead, sharedLink: true })

   if (dto.albumIds && dto.albumIds.length > 0) {
     await this.requireAccess({ auth, ids: dto.albumIds, permission: Permission.AlbumRead });
+  } else if (auth.sharedLink) {
+    throw new BadRequestException('Shared link access is only allowed in combination with an albumIds filter');
   } else {
```

The two e2e tests it shipped check the 400 and check that the allowed case returns the expected id. Neither
can observe the body's metadata, so nothing failed.

## Proof

A link with `showMetadata:false` and `allowDownload:false`. Five sinks redact exactly as intended. Then one
unauthenticated POST with the same key returns latitude 48.8584, longitude 2.2945, city, camera make and
model, `originalFileName`, the full `originalPath` under `/data/upload/<ownerUUID>/`, the checksum and
`ownerId`.

The control that settles the degree of it: a second link on the same album with `showMetadata:true`.

```
ownerId           identical=True
originalFileName  identical=True
lat/lon on showMetadata=FALSE link: 48.8584 / 2.2945
lat/lon on showMetadata=TRUE  link: 48.8584 / 2.2945
```

Byte-identical bodies, zero differing fields. The toggle has no effect on this endpoint at all.

Negative...
